item.title: Miso Katsu: Nagoya's Dark-Sauced Tonkatsu — Guide
item.description: Miso katsu is Nagoya’s answer to tonkatsu: a crisp, golden pork cutlet draped in a glossy deep-brown sauce built on hatcho miso, the intensely savoury soybean miso that has been aged for years in giant cedar barrels near Okazaki since the age of the shoguns. The sauce — sweet, earthy and almost chocolatey in its depth — soaks gently into the panko crust and transforms the dish into the region’s definitive comfort food, served everywhere from the famous Yabaton chain with its pig mascot to old kissaten and department-store restaurants.
